\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2010 SCORING GUIDELINES (Form B)}

\section*{Question 2}

The function \(g\) is defined for \(x>0\) with \(g(1)=2, g^{\prime}(x)=\sin \left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)\), and \(g^{\prime \prime}(x)=\left(1-\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right) \cos \left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find all values of \(x\) in the interval \(0.12 \leq x \leq 1\) at which the graph of \(g\) has a horizontal tangent line.
\item[(b)] On what subintervals of \((0.12,1)\), if any, is the graph of \(g\) concave down? Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) at \(x=0.3\).
\item[(d)] Does the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) at \(x=0.3\) lie above or below the graph of \(g\) for \(0.3<x<1\) ? Why?
\item[(a)] The graph of \(g\) has a horizontal tangent line when \(g^{\prime}(x)=0\). This occurs at \(x=0.163\) and \(x=0.359\).
\item[(b)] \(g^{\prime \prime}(x)=0\) at \(x=0.129458\) and \(x=0.222734\)
The graph of \(g\) is concave down on (0.1295, 0.2227) because \(g^{\prime \prime}(x)<0\) on this interval.
\item[(c)] \(g^{\prime}(0.3)=-0.472161\)
\(g(0.3)=2+\int_{1}^{0.3} g^{\prime}(x) d x=1.546007\)
An equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) is \(y=1.546-0.472(x-0.3)\).
\end{itemize}
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { sets } g^{\prime}(x)=0 \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \text { : answer } \\ 1 \text { : justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\(4:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: g^{\prime}(0.3) \\ 1: \text { integral expression } \\ 1: g(0.3) \\ 1: \text { equation }\end{array}\right.\)
1 : answer with reason
\begin{itemize}
\item[(d)] \(g^{\prime \prime}(x)>0\) for \(0.3<x<1\)
Therefore the line tangent to the graph of \(g\) at \(x=0.3\) lies below the graph of \(g\) for \(0.3<x<1\).
\end{itemize}
